Sofia — taking this on. I generated an initial KMS keyflow draft and annotated where CMK exchange happens for private deployments. Notes:

- Hosted mode: envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS. We hold the master key in a Redwood KMS cluster; data encryption/decryption occurs at the serving node in memory; we do not persist plaintext to disk.
- Private mode: BYOK flow. Customer imports an asymmetric key into their KMS (or we support external HSM). The customer CMK is used to wrap/unwarp per-tenant data keys. The only place customer CMK material is present is in the customer's KMS/HSM; Redwood never sees private key material.
- Network: for Private/Dedicated, traffic traverses customer VPC via AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering; egress is controlled via route tables and egress endpoints. We should advise customers to lock down peering to specific prefix lists.

I attached the draft keyflow and marked two callouts where we should avoid publishing internal subnet IDs. I also added a suggested language snippet for the attestation letter.

[Attachment: kms_keyflow_v1.pdf (PDF, 180 KB)]

1) Attestation: short signed letter on Redwood letterhead confirming production for your account will be hosted only in US (us-west-2) unless you request cross-region migration in writing. This includes our fallback behavior for failover inside the same region and explicit note that we will not route data through other cloud regions.

2) KMS keyflow: two-page diagram (attached) showing Hosted vs Private modes. Key points:
   - Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS (envelope encryption). Data keys are generated per-tenant and wrapped by Redwood master keys. Decrypt/encrypt occurs in-memory on serving nodes; persistent storage contains only wrapped keys and ciphertext.
   - Private: BYOK/CMK — customer retains control of the root key. Per-tenant data keys are wrapped by the customer CMK that never leaves the customer's KMS/HSM. Redwood only receives wrapped data keys.

3) VPC topology: sanitized topology diagram and sample peering snippet. For private deployments we recommend PrivateLink with a NAT-less egress configuration or dedicated egress endpoints under your control. The attached diagram omits internal hostnames and concrete IPs.
